Subject: Follow-up: MedInfex decision path & latency / SLA clarifications

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and asks so we can align internally and with your procurement team: 

1) Decision owners: you mentioned Victor Hale (CTO) as the technical sponsor and someone in procurement for contracts. Can you confirm the economic buyer (VP/Head of Product or Ops) we should engage?

2) Deployment preference: you said private VPC preferred for PHI. Can you confirm whether on-prem is a hard requirement or just considered as an option if the VPC path doesn't meet audit controls?

3) Latency & cost targets: you called out P95 inference latency under 250ms for your user-facing annotator service (1–2 concurrent requests per session). Please confirm targets for batch/async workloads as well and whether cost-per-1k tokens is a gating metric.

4) SLA expectations: do you require contractual SLAs (99.9% uptime) vs. operational SLAs in an SOW? Any specifics on RTO/RPO for outages would help.

Next steps I propose:
- You share procurement contact + any RFI/RFQ templates (we can return a filled RFI within 48 hours).
- We'll run a quick internal mapping: model variant + hosting options + expected unit cost ranges and send back a 1‑pager for Victor and the econ buyer.

Attachments: if you have an RFI template or security checklist we should target, please attach (or point to Drive).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up with Victor + procurement next week if that helps.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — good summary. Quick answers inline: 

1) Economic buyer: please loop in Rana Patel (rana.patel@medinfex.com), VP of Product — she'll lead commercial decisions. Victor will validate technical fit.

2) Deployment: VPC is the preferred path and should satisfy PHI controls if we can meet audit evidence. On-prem would be a last resort; prefer we avoid unless required for certification.

3) Latency: target for interactive annotator is P95 <= 250ms. For nightly batch jobs (bulk inference) SLA is more lenient; we expect throughput targets rather than latency — batch job SLA: complete within a scheduled 4-hour window. Cost: we do track $/1k tokens and will flag if run-rate exceeds budget cap, but it's not an absolute blocker at this stage.

4) SLA: procurement typically asks for a 99.9% availability SLA with clearly defined maintenance windows. RTO expectation is ~2 hours for incident mitigation on production-facing endpoints.

I've attached our RFI template and the security checklist you requested. Procurement contact is procurement@medinfex.com — they own contracting and can share their standard PO/terms.

Attachments: MedInfex_RFI_Template.docx, MedInfex_Security_Checklist.pdf

Happy to set up a 30-min sync with Rana + procurement next Tue or Wed — what times work for your team?

—Alicia
